text:
Maya S: Heads up — starting ~03:00 UTC we saw a spike in Xid 13/31 on a subset of eu-west-1 GPU hosts after last week's host-kernel+driver rollout. Rolling counts: ~40 XIDs in 12h across 8 machines.
Rahul K: Noticed that too. Mostly on g4dn-like instances (p4/rtx-style) — PCI link flaps in dmesg right before the XID.
Elena P: Can you paste the dmesg snippet?
Maya S: Sure, here's an example from host euw-gpu-042:```
[  1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  1234.567892] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  1234.567900] pcieport 0000:2d:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Fatal) error received: id=00e0
```
Sam B: Those AER messages + Xid 31 -> often points at firmware/PCIe training regressions with new kernels or driver combos. Did we change PCIe ASPM or iommu flags in the canary?
Maya S: We bumped kernel from 5.15.0-rc -> 5.15.21 and driver from 525.x -> 535.x in the canary. Only eu-west-1 had the full canary cohort for dedicated hosts (capacity reasons).
Tony L: Capacity note: we cannot drain a lot of eu-west-1 GPUs without violating committed Dedicated SLAs for BigRetail customer during CET daytime.
Lisa R: Can we create a small targeted canary (4 hosts) in a different AZ within eu-west to replicate without hitting reserved racks?
Rahul K: Good idea. I propose: spin 4 hosts in euw-azb, apply kernel+driver combo, attach synthetic workload with our smoke-harness, run a 6h stress that includes prefix caching + long sequence decode (~2k tokens) to exercise KV cache paths.
Elena P: Also add a short PCI stress utility (stresspci) and enable verbose AER logging. We'll capture pcap of PCIe AER events and nvsm dump on XID.
Maya S: Here's the quick checklist I suggest: 1) Isolate 4 hosts not owned by Dedicated commitments 2) Deploy driver 535.86 + kernel 5.15.21 3) Start smoke harness:```
./smoke-harness --workers=8 --seq-len=2048 --duration=6h --kv-cache-load=0.4 --report-interval=5m
```
Sam B: Add metric hooks to push Xid counts, AER counts, ECC corrected/uncc to our ingest. If XIDs > 2 per host in 6h, auto-dump:```
sudo nv-smi --dump-dmesg > /var/log/gpu-dmesg.log
sudo cp /sys/kernel/debug/dri/0/mem_info /tmp/mem_info
```
Infra-Oncall Bot: Deploy job queued: canary-smoke-eu-west-2078901234, target hosts: euw-azb-[12,14,23,27]. ETA provisioning 25m.
Tony L: ETA good — but reminder: we need an ops-approval for any preemptive drains on Dedicated hosts. We'll keep those four outside the Dedicated pool.
Lisa R: If the smoke triggers, what's our rollback plan?
Rahul K: Rollback plan: 1) Remove driver package and boot previous kernel 2) Re-run smoke-harness for 1h to verify stability 3) If still unstable, mark hosts as 'drain-replace' and schedule hardware swaps.
Elena P: We should also run a quick regression test against nv_jit/quantized kernels — some regressions show up only with 16-bit math patterns. Add a short model run that uses mixed-precision.
Maya S: Agree. Also correlating telemetry: list of suspect hosts, last firmware versions, and which racks they belong to. We saw the cluster-scoped spike aligned with a rack-level power-cycler firmware update two nights earlier. Could be correlated.
Sam B: Action items: Rahul+Elena pick hosts and fire the harness, Maya will prepare telemetry dashboard, Tony to confirm capacity carve-out, Lisa to prep ops-approval message if drains required.
Maya S: I'll collect logs and create a postmortem-style doc after the canary. If we see hardware-level faults (ECC uncorrectable) we'll escalate to vendor HW RMA.
Tony L: FYI cost tradeoff — running extended burn-in on spare hosts costs ~4k USD/day in lost throughput vs risk of SLA penalties if we start mass drains. Lean conservative unless we hit >5% of region hosts failing.
Rahul K: Starting provisioning now. I'll ping when canary is up.
Infra-Oncall Bot: canary-smoke-eu-west-2078901234: hosts provisioned, harness started at 2078901450 UTC. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-infra/canaries/2078901234/
Lisa R: Nice. Ping me on results, I'll stand by for ops approval if we need to evacuate any Dedicated capacity. :thumbsup:
